data.title: Paris Court Ruling on Discontinued Feature Will Have Minimal Impact on Angelalign Customers
data.description:
Angelalign Has Already Replaced Torque Ridges with Upgraded "Pressure Points" in Europe

SAN CLEMENTE, Calif., Oct. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Angelalign Technology Inc. (6699.HK) ("Angel") http://www.angelaligner.com, a company driven by innovation in orthodontic clear aligner technology, said today that a ruling by the Paris Local Division of the Unified Patent Court concerning its Torque Ridges feature does not affect the availability of its offering in Europe, which already incorporates the next generation of torque-control technology.

Angel already has discontinued Torque Ridges in Europe and has replaced it with an upgraded feature called Pressure Points. Pressure Points, which launched in the European market in September, was designed to improve torque control and reflects Angel's continued commitment to innovation focused on solving orthodontists' clinical challenges. Angel customers in Spain, the UK and outside of Europe, including the Americas and Asia, are not affected by this ruling. Angel is constantly developing new solutions to continue to serve its customers well.

The court today ruled that the Torque Ridges feature infringes a patent held by Align Technology Inc. (ALGN) for repositioning a patient's teeth according to an orthodontic treatment plan. Angel respectfully disagrees with the decision and is reviewing it closely while it evaluates its options. Angel will comply with the court's ruling, including the return of any products. Because Torque Ridges is no longer offered in Europe, orthodontists using Angel products and services can continue treating their patients with access to Pressure Points and Angel's ongoing clinical and technical support.

"Our priority is to ensure that orthodontists can continue delivering excellent care to their patients," said Xavier Cherbavaz, General Manager and Vice President, Europe, Africa, and the Middle East, Angelalign Technology Inc. "Torque Ridges has already been retired in Europe and replaced with Pressure Points, an approach intended to support controlled force application and tooth contact. We remain focused on giving orthodontists innovative clinical solutions and a dependable customer experience."

"Angel takes intellectual property rights seriously and is careful not to infringe on valid patents," added Richard Hirschland, Angel's Chief Commercial Officer and SVP. "We are reviewing the court's reasoning carefully and will consider all available options. Angel will continue to innovate and improve its products to benefit its providers and their patients despite litigation by a competitor. Continuous innovation means anticipating challenges and preparing solutions to protect the customer experience. Our transition to Pressure Points reflects that commitment. We are determined to continue developing innovative solutions so that orthodontists can rely on Angel over the long term."

To learn more, visit angelaligner.com/eu and www.angelaligner.com.

About Angelalign Technology Inc.

Founded in 2003 and publicly listed since 2021, Angelalign Technology Inc. provides clear aligner solutions to clinically focused professionals and patients in over 60 countries. Having surpassed two million cumulative cases and with about a US$2 billion market capitalization, the company focuses on clinical innovation and professional support to help experts achieve extraordinary outcomes. Its established global operations and continued investment in innovation support its long-term commitment to orthodontists and their patients. Learn more at angelaligner.com.

Angelalign Technology Inc.

sue.kolb@angelaligner.com

data.title: Yields on Treasurys, European Government Bonds Edge Higher — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Emese Bartha and Jessica Fleetham

Yields on U.S. Treasurys and European government bonds edged higher on Friday, pulling away from the multiweek lows reached the previous day.

That advance still left yields below the multidecades highs reached last week. Investors have turned their attention away from concerns about inflation and risks of higher interest rates. Now their focus is on the economic impact of high borrowing costs and the sustainability of debt-funded AI investments.

The 10-year Treasury yield traded at 5.123%, up from an intraday low of 5.068%.

Markets priced in 83% odds of an interest rate hold by the Federal Reserve at its Oct. 28 meeting, up from 72% on Thursday, according to CME, following Chairman Kevin Warsh's remarks during an International Monetary Fund event in Bangkok. Warsh stopped short of giving forward guidance, after officials have indicated in recent days that there is no hurry to hike.

U.S. industrial production rose 0.7% in September after an upwardly revised increase of 0.1% in August. Analysts polled by The Wall Street Journal expected a 0.4% increase last month.

The 10-year German Bund yield was at 3.453%, having hit a five-week low of 3.352% on Thursday.

Bond markets face a "rollercoaster ride" of "one step forward, one step back," pulled by changes in oil prices and risk sentiment, Commerzbank rates strategists said in a note.

Since bond yields globally hit multiyear highs earlier this month, investors have been tempted back into buying government bonds again, particularly given concerns about the sustainability of the AI trade.

"U.S. Treasury yields may have reached levels where their elevated levels weigh on risk sentiment," said Jussi Hiljanen, chief rates strategist at SEB.

Investors are also starting to question whether interest rates will rise as much as markets are currently anticipating. Money markets currently price in up to three rate increases by the Federal Reserve and European Central Bank over the next year, and four by the Bank of England, LSEG data showed.

U.S. rates markets are grappling with two key questions--whether the market is pricing in too many interest-rate hikes over the next year and whether bond yields have peaked, Societe Generale rates strategists said in a note.

The risk of energy prices staying elevated and keeping inflation high remains a concern for bond investors, however.

Inflation remains the pivotal variable for markets because it will influence both the direction of monetary policy and the path of government bond yields, said Laura Lake and Tim Crawmer, senior strategists at Payden & Rygel, in a note.

"If inflation cools more decisively, bonds could deliver price appreciation in addition to income," they said.

Oil prices rose on Friday, with front-month Brent crude up 3% at $109.

  • Paulo Trevisani contributed to this article.

Write to Emese Bartha at emese.bartha@wsj.com and Jessica Fleetham at jessica.fleetham@wsj.com

data.title: RBI approves merger of Emirates NBD's India branches with RBL Bank from 1 December
data.description:
MUMBAI, Oct. 16 -- The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has approved the merger of Emirates NBD Bank P.J.S.C.'s Indian branches with RBL Bank, effective 1 December, consolidating the two banks' Indian operations after the Dubai-based lender acquired a majority stake in the private sector bank earlier this year.

The approval brings Emirates NBD's three Indian branches under RBL Bank, following the completion of an over Rs.26,000 crore transaction that made the foreign lender the promoter of RBL Bank.

"RBI sanctioned the Scheme of Amalgamation of Indian branches of Emirates NBD Bank P.J.S.C. (Transferor Bank) with RBL Bank Limited (Transferee Bank)," the central bank said in a release, adding that all Indian branches of Emirates NBD will function as branches of RBL Bank from 1 December 2026.

The RBI announcement came post market hours. Shares of RBL Bank ended 1.1% higher today at Rs.378.25 on the National Stock Exchange.

On 18 June, Emirates NBD completed its acquisition of a 60% stake in RBL Bank for Rs.26,000 crore, making it the bank's promoter. The transaction also included the appointment of five Emirates NBD executives as additional non-executive, non-independent directors on RBL Bank's board.

The deal was first announced in October 2025, when Emirates NBD said it would acquire a majority stake for $3 billion, or over Rs.26,000 crore. The transaction was billed as the largest-ever foreign direct investment and equity fundraise in India's banking sector. Shareholders approved the deal in November 2025, followed by RBI approval in April 2026 for Emirates NBD to acquire up to 74% of RBL Bank.

The Dubai government, through Investment Corp. of Dubai and Dubai Holding Group, holds about 56% in Emirates NBD. Listed on the Dubai Financial Market, the bank has a market capitalization of more than $50 billion. In India, it operates as a wholly owned subsidiary, with three branches in Mumbai, Gurugram and Chennai and around 30 employees.

RBL Bank, by comparison, had 628 branches and 14,222 employees, catering to over 15 million customers, at the end of September 2026. Managing director and chief executive officer R. Subramaniakumar told Mint in October 2025 that branch expansion would be one of the biggest areas of deployment for the new capital.

On 12 October, RBL Bank reported a net profit of Rs.4,818 crore for the second quarter of fiscal year 2027 (Q2FY27), up 170% year-on-year and 90% sequentially. Net advances rose 42% year-on-year and 22% quarter-on-quarter to Rs.1.4 trillion at the end of September, while deposits increased 34% year-on-year and 25% sequentially to Rs.1.6 trillion.

In a post-earnings analyst call same day, Subramaniakumar said the capital infusion and change in ownership would help RBL Bank deepen existing relationships and establish new ones with large corporates that had previously been inaccessible because of constraints related to credit ratings, capital or the bank's cost of funds.

The bank is also targeting trade flows along corridors where Emirates NBD operates, seeking to gain a "competitive advantage because of Emirates NBD's network". At the same time, it plans to build granular and stable liabilities to progressively narrow the gap between its cost of deposits and that of larger banks.

"We want to leverage the momentum from the FCNR (foreign currency non-resident) deposit relationship we have onboarded to target non-resident flows, starting with the Middle East, and over time, in all the geographies where Emirates NBD has a presence," he said.

RBL Bank also plans to invest in its distribution infrastructure, including branches, people and technology, to strengthen its presence in relevant geographies and roll out a wealth proposition for customers.

Subramaniakumar said the bank aims to add 30-50 branches every quarter. Expansion, however, will involve more than increasing the branch count: RBL Bank also plans to "densify" existing branches by adding employees at locations where staff have reached the "desired level" of productivity.

"We are going to have a differentiated approach, which is going to be unique for us, in the sense that we are entering into the affluent, which we said almost 3-4 quarters before that we are getting into the wealth business. Now, with the Emirates NBD partnership, we are pretty confident of expanding this growth."

Brokerages differed on how quickly RBL Bank can translate its capital infusion and expanding franchise into stronger returns.

"Much of the improvement (in margins and cost to income ratio) has come from equity infusion by Emirates NBD and the FCNR(B) mobilization, which together grew the balance sheet 20% QoQ," HDFC Securities said in a note.

While excess capital and liquidity offer medium-term tailwinds for growth and net interest margin, the bank needs to use this window to address its "structural handicaps", the brokerage said. It maintained a 'Reduce' rating on the stock, with a target price of Rs.300.

Emkay Global Financial, by contrast, raised its price target by 10.5% to Rs.475 and maintained a 'buy' rating, citing expectations that return on assets (RoA) would gradually improve to 1-1.3% over FY27-FY29. RBL Bank reported RoA of 0.92% for the quarter, while return on equity (RoE) stood at 4.43%.

"We find RBL as uniquely positioned amongst the fastest growing banks (30% CAGR) along with an improving franchise (lower cost of funds, rising branches)," ICICI Securities said in a post-earnings note. A shift in product mix towards secured loans could weigh on margins but help ease credit costs, it added. The brokerage expects RoA to improve to 1.4%, while RoE is likely to remain in single digits because of low leverage.

data.title: Cult.fit IPO alert: Fitness major receives SEBI nod for proposed IPO - Check OFS, fresh issue mix details
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 16 -- Cult.fit IPO: Months after filing draft papers, fitness services firm Cult.fit received Securities Exchange Board of India (SEBI)'s approval for the initial public offering on Friday. Apart from approving the IPO, the market watchdog has issued observations on the company's Draft Red Herring Prospectus (DRHP).

Apart from Cult.fit, Sohan Lal Commodity Management, Eswari Global Metal Industries and Indian Gas Exchange (IGX) also received SEBI nod to proceed with their IPO plans.

Cult.fit filed to bring its IPO in July. The fitness major aims to raise nearly 9.5 billion rupees through a combination of fresh issues and offer for sale (OFS).

The proposed IPO is a combination of a fresh issue, a component to create and sell new shares to the public, and an offer for sale (OFS), a mechanism for existing shareholders to sell their shares. The proposed IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to Rs.950 crore and an OFS of up to 17.86 crore equity shares by existing shareholders.

There is no information available about the price band, and timeline of Cult.fit's proposed IPO.

The Bengaluru-headquartered fitness firm operates 708 fitness centres across India and had more than 987000 paid members as of March 31, 2026. The company had filed its IPO papers in July this year.

The firm would use the proceeds to fund new centres, including its app and website, corporate partnership programmes and direct sales at its fitness centres.

The funds raised via IPO would be utilised to expand with new centres. The company will also use the amount for branding and marketing expenses.

Cult.fit sells memberships through multiple channels, including its app and website, corporate partnership programmes and direct sales at its fitness centres. The book lead running managers for the proposed IPO are Axis Capital and Goldman Sachs.

data.title: This small-cap AI stock has surged 250% in 2026: What is behind its stellar market performance?
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 16 -- In a year marked by a sharp sell-off triggered by heightened tensions in the Middle East, some small-cap stocks have managed to withstand the selling pressure, with E2E Networks being one of them.

The stock has been marching higher since the start of the year after witnessing a brutal sell-off throughout 2025. So far this year, the stock has risen from Rs.199 to Rs.694, resulting in a massive gain of 248%.

This performance marks a sharp contrast to the 50% decline recorded in the previous year. While demand for software stocks has remained muted, E2E Networks has benefited from rising demand for AI infrastructure and has also signed deals involving NVIDIA.

The company is an NSE-listed, MeitY-empanelled, AI-focused hyperscale cloud platform offering advanced cloud GPUs and a comprehensive ecosystem of cloud technologies designed to support the development and deployment of AI, machine learning (ML), and generative AI (GenAI) workloads on large-scale compute clusters.

During the September quarter, the company signed a binding term sheet worth approximately Rs.1,000 crore, excluding taxes, with an Indian sovereign AI company for NVIDIA Blackwell cloud GPUs and allied services. The agreement is valid through June 2029.

The company also enhanced its TIR AI/ML platform by adding VPC Connect, which enables secure, private networking for GPU instances, training clusters, and inference endpoints.

The feature provides enterprise-grade isolation across the AI lifecycle for regulated workloads, comparable to that offered by global hyperscalers.

Through Jarvislabs.ai, its AI cloud platform, the company introduced managed endpoints and model APIs, offering production-ready open-weight models and pay-per-token APIs for open-source models.

Infrastructure upgrades during the quarter included InfiniBand H200 clusters, serverless inference that scales to zero, private VPC networking, object storage, and shared file systems.

The company today posted delivered strong performance for the September quarter, with revenue rising to Rs.223.8 crore, showing a 411% year-on-year and 43% quarter-on-quarter, driven by contributions from Blackwell GPUs, improved utilization, and higher average realizations across the GPU fleet.

EBITDA margin expanded to 76.6%, while profit before tax (PBT) grew 66% sequentially to Rs.97.1 crore. On the bottom line, the net profit jumped 32.5% to Rs.72.7 crore.

"For Q2 FY27, revenue increased 5.1 times year-on-year to Rs.223.8 crore, EBITDA margin expanded further to 76.6%, and profit after tax (PAT) rose to Rs.72.7 crore. The approximately Rs.1,000 crore sovereign AI contract for Blackwell GPUs provides strong revenue visibility through 2029," the company said in its filing.

With shareholder approval for growth capital in place, the company remains focused on aggressive yet judicious capacity expansion to meet India's growing demand for AI compute, the company said in its regulatory filing.

data.title: XOM Stock Climbs On $4.5B Refining Lift Estimate; Goldman Sees Q3 EPS Exceeding Wall Street Expectations
data.description:
Key points:
  • The company said it saw no volume losses tied to Middle East events in the third quarter.
  • Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta said the filing implied Q3 earnings per share near $4.10.
  • Exxon is slated to announce full results for the quarter on Oct. 30.

Shares of ExxonMobil (XOM) advanced modestly on Friday after the company said that higher refining margins could add about $4.5 billion to third-quarter results compared with the prior quarter.

As of the time of writing, XOM traded 2% higher at about $178.04.

What Did Exxon Say?

In the second quarter, Exxon’s adjusted earnings stood at $14.7 billion. Compared with the prior quarter, estimated market effects in the third quarter include a $1.3 billion hit from lower oil and liquids prices in the production business, a $0.3 billion gain from higher natural gas prices, and a net $4.4 billion boost from better product margins, the company said in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

Margin improvement is expected to come mainly from a $4.5 billion rise in the refining and fuels business, partly offset by a $0.6 billion decline in chemicals and a $0.5 billion gain in specialty products.

Other planned and seasonal factors included a $0.2 billion benefit from less scheduled maintenance, a $0.6 billion drag from outside disruptions to operations, a $0.3 billion lift from having more days in the third quarter, and a $0.9 billion reduction in the production business from items such as contract entitlements and sales timing. The company said it saw no volume losses tied to Middle East events in the quarter.

Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta said the filing implied earnings per share near $4.10. That sits above FactSet consensus of roughly $3.87, but below the firm’s own $4.33 estimate, it said. Goldman holds a ‘Neutral’ rating and a $169 price target on the shares. Exxon is slated to announce full results for the quarter on Oct. 30.

How Did XOM Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around XOM stock stayed within the bearish territory over the past 24 hours, while message volume stayed at normal levels.

A Stocktwits user cheered the stock approaching its 52-week high of $178.69.

data.title: Micron Stock's Drop Triggers 'Buy the Dip' Calls. No One's Listening. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Adam Clark

Micron Technology stock is well off its highs. That's an opportunity to buy into the memory-chip company before the next round of price increases, according to Wall Street analysts.

The shares were down 3.5% at $899.15 in early trading. Although the price has more than tripled this year so far, it has slumped from its summer peak of more than $1,200.

The recent causes have been fears of memory-chip competition from China's CXMT and doubts about the sustainability of the artificial-intelligence boom in general.

But the CXMT-driven fall this week is just giving investors "another reason to buy the memory dip," according to Kent Fung, vice president for market intelligence at Fundstrat. He noted that CXMT's so-called 4F square design could challenge conventional server dynamic random access memory (DRAM), but it is not competition for the high-bandwidth memory (HBM) demanded for AI servers.

"Investors should consider the possibility that the knee-jerk response to CXMT's announcement has been a bit of an overreaction," Fung wrote in a research note Thursday.

"While CXMT's DRAM breakthrough is impressive, it has a weaker association with AI and thus, arguably weaker implications for memory and storage stocks, particularly with regard to their growth potential," he added.

Fung is not alone in his optimism. KeyBanc analyst John Vinh reiterated a $1,750 target price on Micron and called it one of his favorite ideas following a trip to check supply chains in Asia. His findings included that pricing for DRAM in the fourth quarter is expected to rise by 15%-20% from the previous quarter and Google is looking at extending long-term memory-supply agreements through to 2035.

"While we do not believe that the current memory upcycle will extend to 2031 or 2035, this would suggest customers are concerned that the memory shortages are going to persist for an extended period of time and at least beyond 2028," Vinh wrote in a Thursday research note.

data.title: Drilling to Start at Coyote Copper's Arizona Copper Project the First Half of November and 97.7% of the Accelerated Warrants Were Exercised
data.description:
Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - October 16, 2026) - Coyote Copper Mines Inc.  ("Coyote Copper" or the "Company ") is pleased to announce that it has signed a drilling contract to commence drilling the first half of November.

Warrant Acceleration

As of October 15, 2026 at 4:00 pm the following Warrants were exercised

  • 7,311,901 Warrants with an exercise price of $0.15 from a financing that was completed in July and August of 2025 were exercised.
  • 10,622,351 Warrants with an exercise price of $0.20 from a financing that was completed in January and February of 2026 were exercised.
  • 1,052,152 finder's Warrants with an exercise price of $0.14 from a financing that was completed in January and February of 2026 were exercised.
  • The total amount received by the Company from the exercising of the Warrants was C$3,368,556.63
  • 97.7% of the Warrants were exercised.

The money received from the Warrant exercise will help fund the ongoing and planned exploration program, and fund additional mining claims being staked and acquired.

Exploration Update

  • The previously announced geophysical programs will be completed shortly. Once completed and interpreted, the company shall release the results.
  • Soil and channel sampling continue, results will be disseminated prior to drilling.
  • Drill roads and pads are being built, all necessary permits are in hand.
  • Drilling to start the first half of November. The drill slated for our program is finishing up another company's project, so the exact date for our drilling to start is not known yet.

Dan Weir, CEO of Coyote Copper Mines Inc., stated: "We are very excited to see the drilling begin in approximately 20 to 30 days. The geophysics programs are yielding great results. We completed a site visit at the end of November which 35 people attended including 4 geologists from major mining and fund companies and numerous investors. Having 97.75% of the Warrants exercised, shows that our investors believe in the company, and the work we are doing. I would like to acknowledge all the amazing work that our geologists and geophysical contractors are completing. The large mining companies that have visited the project, have positively commented on the professional work."

data.title: AI Fears Are Rocking Markets. The Brave Should Buy the Dips. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Alex Rosenberg

In the words of Elon Musk: "Yikes."

This past week, investors questioned some of the core ideas undergirding the artificial-intelligence trade, and the market action got ugly. That could make this a golden opportunity to buy the dip in chips and other AI enablers.

We're not trying to minimize the concerns. The spectacular rise in interest rates — which saw the 10-year Treasury yield hitting 5.36% earlier this month before cooling off — has led to increasing skepticism about the outlook for debt-reliant companies. CoreWeave, which rents out computing capacity to AI model companies, saw the yields on its bonds rise to above 15% (and its stock plunge by about 25% on the week), which earned that "yikes" from the world's first trillionaire.

"This isn't the first time we've had a sizable market wobble on the back of AI fears, but as we move to a capex cycle funded out of debt rather than simply free cash flow, we have to increasingly respect the credit price action," writes Deutsche Bank's Jim Reid.

In other words: a massive amount of capital will be needed for the AI buildout, and higher rates and wider credit spreads will make it that much more expensive for companies to tap the credit markets.

The AI crowd is also looking to equity markets, with OpenAI and Anthropic both planning to go public. But there, too, we're seeing problems. It was reported this past week that Anthropic grew revenue by 45% in the third quarter over the second quarter, which is obviously impressive. But that's down from the triple-digit quarter-over-quarter growth seen in the second quarter, leading to concerns about Anthropic's valuation.

Just as the market was trying to come to grips with AI financing concerns, "the outlined revenue profile of Anthropic underwhelmed, further dampening any AI momentum," writes Evercore ISI's Nicholas Amicucci.

Anthropic and OpenAI support a large share of the AI ecosystem, and they might well make the best AI models. But if other models are nearly as good, then companies and consumers won't be willing to pay up for Claude and ChatGPT. And then who will pay for the data centers and the chips?

So the semiconductors have had a dreadful run, with the iShares Semiconductor exchange-traded fund falling for nine straight sessions to lose 15%. There's no need to send its holders a condolence basket, though, given that the ETF remains 60% higher on the year.

In fact, one of the themes this week has been that the winning stocks have suffered, while the losers have enjoyed a rare moment in the sun. Hated names like Cava Group, Lululemon Athletica, and Nike all rallied powerfully on Thursday and Friday. The consumer staples sector — previously highlighted in this column as the best hedge against an AI slowdown — rose 5% on the week.

As a result, index performance varied wildly. The Nasdaq Composite fell 4.3% on the week, while the S&P 500 lost just 1.9%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average was actually 0.5% higher.

One of the clearest ways to make sense of the action is to look at the iShares MSCI USA Momentum Factor ETF, which tracks the market's best performers. It fell every day of the week, losing 8%, for its worst run since July. Back then, the carnage was precipitated by forced selling on the part of AI-focused Situational Awareness hedge fund — and unconfirmed rumors of another AI-related fund blowing up were getting passed around on Thursday.

The broader point is that the AI winners have become very popular hedge fund holdings, which means that sharp declines can be met with forced selling, begetting further declines. Since such funds generally hedge their exposure, they will pair longs in semiconductors with short trades on stocks like Nike and Cava.

Long/short story short: There are fundamental reasons to be concerned about the AI trade right now, but positioning is running the show.

"Fear is in the air," writes Warren Pies of 3Fourteen Research. "Whether or not it is prudent to reduce risk, this backdrop requires more tactical positioning and an extra dose of paranoia."

Or, as Baird tech strategist Ted Mortonson tells us: "You don't catch a falling knife until it hits the ground and stops spinning."

Mortonson sees tremendous potential in AI and in many of the AI enablers, particularly names like Microsoft and ServiceNow, which help other companies integrate and use AI, and are trading at reasonable valuations. "They already have their hooks into the enterprise, which means the game is theirs to lose," he says.

But he emphasizes that when the selling gets heavy, the wise seek out higher ground.

"Until this market gets rooted back in the fundamentals," Mortonson says, "I'm just buying Berkshire."

It's a sound strategy. But for those readers who have been waiting on the sidelines to buy an AI dip — well, what are you waiting for?

Write to Alex Rosenberg at alex.rosenberg@barrons.com

data.title: US fiscal 2026 budget deficit rises to $1.99 trillion, largest in 5 years
data.description:
The US budget deficit rose by $217 billion to $1.99 trillion in the 2026 fiscal year, fueled in part by tariff refunds and record spending to service the nation's more-than $40 trillion in debt, marking the largest budget shortfall in five years, Treasury Department figures reported on Friday showed.

The results for the year ended September 30, the first full budget year of President Donald Trump's second term, compared to a $1.78 trillion deficit in fiscal 2025. It was the largest shortfall since fiscal 2021's $2.77 trillion budget gap, then fueled by COVID-19 pandemic relief spending, and is the third- largest annual deficit ever.

Total receipts for fiscal 2026 were a record $5.40 trillion, up $169 billion, or 3%, from the $5.24 trillion in fiscal 2025. Fiscal 2026 outlays also were a record at $7.40 trillion, up $386 billion, or 6%, from the $7.01 trillion in the prior fiscal year.

Debt-service outlays totaled a record $1.36 trillion, climbing by $144 billion, or 12%, a spending category now eclipsed only by Social Security and the combined outlays for Medicare and Medicaid. Total US debt breached the $40 trillion milestone about two months ago.

Another driver of the widening shortfall was a $22 billion drop in net tariff receipts following a Supreme Court ruling this year negating a large portion of the tariffs Trump had imposed during his first year in office. That triggered $145 billion of tariff refunds over this year, resulting in an 11% decline in net tariff income to about $173 billion.

A U.S. Treasury official said the department calculated an estimated deficit-to-GDP ratio of 6.2% for fiscal 2026, but declined to say what GDP estimate was used. This figure compares to an actual 5.8% deficit-to-GDP ratio for fiscal 2025.

For the 2026 fiscal year's final month of September, the Treasury reported a deficit of $27 billion versus a $198 billion surplus a year earlier.

data.title: Novartis halts mid-stage trial for kidney drug, Fabhalta, in lupus nephritis
data.description:
Novartis has terminated a mid-stage trial for its oral Factor B inhibitor Fabhalta (iptacopan) in lupus nephritis, an inflammatory condition affecting the kidneys, because of strategic considerations, according to a federal database on clinical studies.

In an Oct. 15 update, the company said that it was no longer looking for enrollees for the two-part study, which evaluated the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of iptacopan (LNP023) with standard of care in 81 patients with LN.

Approved for multiple complement-mediated diseases, including primary immunoglobulin A nephropathy, Fabhalta generated roughly $505M in sales for the company last year, with over 150% YoY growth in Q4 on a currency-adjusted basis. Endpoints News first reported about the discontinuation.

The Swiss pharma giant has faced a string of late-stage trial setbacks lately, including for its RNA-based therapy del-desiran against a rare muscle-wasting disease called myotonic dystrophy type 1 in September. That came days after another late-stage trial failure for pelacarsen, a heart disease therapy it developed with Ionis Pharmaceuticals .

data.title: Deforestation in Brazil's Amazon falls to lowest on record in 2025/26
data.description:
Deforestation in Brazil's Amazon rainforest declined to the lowest level on record in the 12 months through July, data released by Brazilian space research agency Inpe showed on Friday.

  • Some 3,335 square kilometers (1,287.65 square miles) of Amazon jungle were destroyed in the 12 months through July, down about 42% from the previous period

  • It is the lowest deforestation level on record in the historical series that goes back to 1988, the data showed

  • The data is produced yearly by Inpe's PRODES satellite monitoring program

  • The official annual period is measured from August to July as there is less cloud cover in the middle of the year to obscure deforestation on satellite images

  • In Brazil's Cerrado savanna, deforestation fell about 24% in the period, to some 5,517 square kilometers, also the lowest on record — in this case the series goes back to 2001

data.title: Opus Genetics Secures FDA Approval For Eye Drops – Set To Receive Milestone Payment
data.description:
Key points:
  • Ryzumvi contains phentolamine ophthalmic solution 0.75%, which reduces pupil size to improve near vision without affecting longer-distance vision.
  • The approval was supported by two Phase 3 trials.
  • Opus is studying Ryzumvi for vision problems in dim lighting after laser eye surgery.

Opus Genetics (IRD) was in the spotlight on Friday, after the U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved its eye drop for treating presbyopia, an age-related condition that makes it difficult to focus on nearby objects.

The approval expands the use of an already commercialized therapy and triggers a milestone payment from commercial partner Viatris (VTRS).

At the time of writing, IRD shares were trading 3.4% lower, while VTRS stock gained about 1%.

Approval Based On Two Phase 3 Trials

Opus’ Ryzumvi contains phentolamine ophthalmic solution 0.75%, which reduces pupil size to improve near vision without affecting longer-distance vision. The approval was supported by two Phase 3 trials, VEGA-2 and VEGA-3, which met their primary and key secondary goals without serious treatment-related side effects.

Notably, 27.2% of patients receiving the eye drop saw an improvement of at least 15 letters (three lines) on an eye chart, compared with 11.5% receiving a placebo.

The drug previously received FDA approval in September 2023 to reverse pupil dilation caused by medications used during eye examinations. Viatris launched it commercially in April 2024.

The companies’ licensing agreement dates back to November 2022, when Ocuphire Pharma, which acquired Opus in October 2024, granted Viatris the rights to commercialize the treatment.

The agreement included $35 million upfront, up to $130 million in milestone payments, and royalties.

IRD Finances To Support Operations Into 2029

Opus is developing gene therapies for inherited retinal diseases, including OPGx-BEST1 for Best disease and OPGx-LCA5 for severe inherited vision loss. The company is also studying Ryzumvi for vision problems in dim lighting following laser eye surgery.

Opus reported $88.8 million in cash and cash equivalents as of June 30, and has a financing option of up to $120 million under an agreement with Oberland Capital. The company expects its cash position to support operations into 2029.

IRD, VTRS See Strong Gains In 2026

Retail sentiment surrounding both IRD on Stocktwits flipped to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘neutral’ over the past 24 hours, amid ‘high’ message volumes. Meanwhile, sentiment for VTRS remained ‘neutral’.

IRD shares have seen strong buying interest so far this year, surging 84%. Meanwhile, VTRS stock has gained about 48%.

data.title: Star Health Brings 'Bishram Grih' and Face Scan Health Assessments to Durga Puja Pandals in Kolkata and Durgapur
data.description:
First-of-its-kind initiative by Star Health offers pandal hoppers in Kolkata and Durgapur a comfortable space to rest and refresh, along with an instant indicative health report covering approximately 17 parameters

KOLKATA, India, Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Limited () (BSE: 543412), one of India's leading standalone health insurance companies, today announced the introduction of 'Bishram Grih' at select Durga Puja pandals in Kolkata and Durgapur. The first-of-its-kind initiative by Star Health offers pandal hoppers a comfortable lounge-style space to "Rest, Relax & Rejuvenate" during their Puja journey. Each Bishram Grih will also feature a technology-led Face Scan health assessment, enabling visitors to gain quick insights into select health indicators.

Pandal hopping during Durga Puja can be tiring, particularly for those visiting multiple locations in a day. At each Bishram Grih, visitors can take a break, sit comfortably and enjoy refreshments such as tea and water before continuing their Puja journey.

A key feature of the Bishram Grih is Star Health's Face Scan health assessment kiosk. Through a simple and contactless facial scan, visitors can receive an instant indicative health report covering approximately 17 health parameters. The assessment provides insights into select vital signs and indicators related to stress, recovery and heart rate variability, including heart rate, respiratory rate, stress index and HRV metrics, among others.

Star Health will set up two Bishram Grihs in Kolkata and one in Durgapur. The initiative will be active from 16 October to 20 October 2026 at the following Puja pandals:

  • Bag bazar Sarbojanin Durgotsav Exhibition, Kolkata
  • 22 Palli Sarodotsab, Northern Park, Kolkata
  • Marconi Dakshina Pally, Durgapur

Operating hours: 11AM onwards

Commenting on the initiative, Mr. Himanshu Walia, Whole-time Director & CMO, Star Health Insurance, said, ""Durga Puja is a festival close to every Bengali's heart, and pandal hopping is an integral part of the celebrations. With thousands of people spending long hours visiting pandals, we wanted to create a space where they could pause, rest and recharge before continuing their Puja journey. Bishram Grih brings this thought to life by offering visitors a comfortable lounge-style space with refreshments at select pandals in Kolkata and Durgapur.

By integrating a quick and contactless Face Scan health assessment into the experience, we are also encouraging visitors to become more aware of select health indicators in a simple and accessible manner. Through Bishram Grih, we hope to combine festive convenience with preventive health awareness and make wellbeing a meaningful part of the Durga Puja experience."

Star Health also encourages pandal hoppers in Kolkata and Durgapur, particularly senior citizens and families with young children, to take precautions during the festivities. These include staying hydrated, taking regular breaks between pandal visits, wearing comfortable footwear and seeking medical advice in case of any discomfort.

Commenting on the regional initiative, Mr. Atin Roy, Business Head - West Bengal, Star Health Insurance, said, "West Bengal comes alive during Durga Puja, with families and visitors spending long hours exploring pandals across the region. Bishram Grih responds to a practical need by offering pandal hoppers a comfortable space to pause, refresh and regain energy. Visitors can also access a complimentary, contactless Face Scan health assessment that provides an instant indicative report covering approximately 17 health parameters. By setting up these facilities at prominent pandals in Kolkata and Durgapur, we aim to make comfort and health awareness a meaningful part of the festive experience."

By bringing together physical comfort and preventive health awareness, Bishram Grih seeks to make wellbeing a meaningful part of the Durga Puja experience. Through such technology-led initiatives, Star Health is exploring ways to complement health insurance protection with solutions that encourage people to remain more engaged with their overall wellbeing.

With customer-centricity at its core, the Company has developed superior and innovative product offerings, service capabilities and a seamless claims management process. data.title: HPE Stock's Worst Week Ever Exposes Wall Street's Newest Fear — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Kit Norton

Broader market pressure on tech stocks and concerns around the artificial-intelligence trade are both valid reasons behind Hewlett Packard Enterprise's worst week ever. But an analyst's downgrade revealed a potentially deeper problem for the highflying stock.

HPE has more than doubled this year, rising 134% despite the recent rough patch. Shares declined 4% to $56.24 in Friday midday trading and aredown more than 23% for the week. If the move holds through the closing bell, that would be HPE's worst-ever weekly performance. The last time HPE stock fell this hard was the week of March 7, 2025 when it declined 20%.

Hewlett-Packard Company split into two entities in 2015: HP Inc. and HPE, which makes servers, storage, and other information technology infrastructure.

A stock downgrade earlier in the week triggered the selloff. Barclays analyst Tim Long on Wednesday downgraded HPE along with Dell Technologies and NetApp to Equal Weight from Overweight. The firm lowered its price target on HPE to $77 down from $83.

Long said he was taking a more cautious approach on those stocks. Their valuations have soared this year as sky-high memory costs boosted revenue. Booming demand for AI has led to a memory chip supply crunch and rising costs for memory.

His concern is that the revenue gains for HPE and others reflect higher memory prices more than growing adoption of enterprise AI, a distinction that matters for investors assessing whether the gains can continue.

The analyst added that HPE and other hardware stocks don't appear to have a "meaningful AI inflection" that could produce product adoption, enhanced business performance, and significant revenue growth.

Morgan Stanley analyst Erik Woodring offered a similar assessment Monday, saying higher memory pricing was the main driver of the current hardware cycle.

Woodring said he was "waiting for evidence" of an AI inflection point and that recent surveys suggest accelerated hardware spending was primarily cyclical and not AI-driven.

Wall Street expects increased memory prices to continue into 2027, but the fear is clear. If the shortage ends, future weeks may look even worse.
